findings.evidence: upstream/Physlib/Physlib/Relativity/LorentzGroup/Rotations.lean:189 `lemma toVector_rotation {d} (Λ : Rotations d)`; ibid. :181 `lemma rotations_subset_restricted (d) : Rotations d ≤ LorentzGroup.restricted d`.
findings.fix: Rename to `rotation_inr_inl_eq_zero`, `rotation_inl_inr_eq_zero`, `timeComponent_rotation_smul`, `spatialPart_rotation_smul_apply`, and update the four uses in PhaseSpace.lean (lines 391, 399, 414) and the module docstring.
findings.issue: `rotations_inr_inl_0`, `rotations_inl_0_inr`, `timeComponent_rotations_smul` and `spatialPart_rotations_smul_apply` (lines 27, 32, 39, 46) all take a single `Λ : Rotations d`, but use the plural `rotations`, which upstream denotes the subgroup. Physlib's own element-level lemma is `toVector_rotation (Λ : Rotations d)`; the plural appears only in `rotations_subset_restricted (d) : Rotations d ≤ ...`. The docstrings here say "of a rotation" (singular), so the names contradict them. Since this module is at the PhyslibAlpha mirror path and is meant to land next to `toVector_rotation` without renaming, the inconsistency ships upstream.

findings.evidence: upstream/Physlib/Physlib/Relativity/LorentzGroup/Boosts/Apply.lean:28,36,44; the statements are `(Λ : LorentzGroup d).1 (Sum.inr j) (Sum.inl 0) = 0` (line 28) and `... (Sum.inl 0) (Sum.inr j) = 0` (line 33).
findings.fix: Drop the index `0` (there is only one `Sum.inl` index, since the row type is `Fin 1 ⊕ Fin d`) and name the conclusion: `rotation_inr_inl_eq_zero` and `rotation_inl_inr_eq_zero`.
findings.issue: `rotations_inr_inl_0` and `rotations_inl_0_inr` end in `_0`, which names the column/row index `Sum.inl 0`, not the conclusion; read as a Mathlib name the trailing `_0` reads as the value of the entry, and the actual conclusion (`= 0`) is unstated. Physlib's entry lemmas for the same matrices carry a conclusion suffix (`boost_time_eq`, `boost_inr_self_eq`, `boost_inr_other_eq`).

summary: Names in the main file describe their conclusions and follow the local and Mathlib conventions; no new notation is introduced. The four lemmas in RotationsExtensions.lean, which is written to be moved into PhyslibAlpha unrenamed, use the plural subgroup name where the adjacent upstream lemma uses the singular, and two of them end in `_0` (an index) where the conclusion is `= 0`.
